title: a carpenter's son from a nowhere town, not a stained-glass window
hook: a carpenter's son from a nowhere town, not a stained-glass window
carry: he ate with the wrong people on purpose

segments.voice: Two words in. Amen, a yes. Grace, a gift you didn't earn. Your line was: you are already held. Did you pause before a meal? Day three.

Think of the pictures of Jesus you've seen. A stained-glass window, lit from behind. A painting with a golden circle around his head. A calm face on a card in a hospital waiting room. Now try this instead. A man with rough hands. Sawdust, or stone dust, on his clothes. A local accent people from the city would have laughed at. A family everybody in the village knew by name. When he started to teach, the neighbors weren't impressed. They were confused. Isn't that just the builder? Christians believe a great deal about who he was. But the Gospels start somewhere very ordinary, and so does today.
screen: `NOT A STAINED-GLASS WINDOW.` → `ROUGH HANDS. A LOCAL ACCENT.` → `ISN'T THAT JUST THE BUILDER?`

segments.voice: Start with the name. Jesus is the English form of a Greek name, which comes from the Hebrew Yeshua, the same name as Joshua. It was common. It means, roughly, God saves. Plenty of boys in his village could have answered to it. Then the job. When he comes home and teaches, Mark's Gospel has the neighbors ask, in the King James words: "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?" Matthew has it: "Is not this the carpenter's son?" The Greek word is tekton. A builder, a craftsman. It could mean wood, and it could mean stone. Either way: a working man with a trade. Then the town. Nazareth was a small village in Galilee, off the main roads. When a man named Nathanael first hears where Jesus is from, he says: "Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?" And his friend Philip answers with three words: "Come and see." Here's what surprised people most. Not where he came from. Who he sat down with. In Mark's Gospel he eats at the house of a tax collector, a man who worked for Rome and was widely resented, with a table full of people others avoided. Some religious teachers watching ask his followers how he can eat with tax collectors and sinners. His answer: healthy people don't need a doctor. Sick people do. In that world, sharing a table said: you belong with me. He shared it with the wrong people, and he did it on purpose. Christians say much more about Jesus: that he is the Son of God, that he died and rose again. The path gets to all of that. It starts at a table.
screen: `YESHUA — A COMMON NAME.` · `TEKTON — A BUILDER.` · `NAZARETH — COME AND SEE.` · `A TABLE WITH THE WRONG PEOPLE.` · then, large: `IT STARTS AT A TABLE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Three breaths, with the bell. On the first, picture a table. Any table you've eaten at. On the second, notice who is usually sitting at it. On the third, picture one person who usually isn't. Someone you'd never think to invite. Just give them a chair, in your mind, for one breath. If you pray, you can bring them with you into it.
Jesus. Yeshua. A builder's name from a small town, the name at the center of the whole Christian path. Third word.
Your line: he ate with the wrong people on purpose. Today, sit with someone you usually wouldn't. At lunch, on a call, for five minutes. That's day three.

howItsDone: Christians come to know Jesus mainly through the four Gospels, read aloud in church services, and many pray to him or in his name every day.

fork.setup: you're a teacher in Galilee. a tax collector, a man people resent, invites you to dinner with his friends. what do you do?
options: decline politely, to keep your good name.
go, and sit down at the table.
send a message to him instead.
fork.reveal: Jesus went. when asked why, he said healthy people don't need a doctor; sick people do. the table was the point.

original.note: Hebrew and Aramaic. the same name as Joshua. Greek wrote it Iēsous, and English got Jesus.

trapdoor: what you thought: the face in the stained-glass window.
what it means: a builder's son from a small town, who ate with the people others avoided.
what a scholar hears: tekton, a builder in wood or stone; Yeshua, one of the most common names of his day.
